statement.p: A point is chosen at random from the region S in the xy-plane containing all points (x,y) such that -2\le x\le 2, -1\le y\le 1 and x - y\le 0 (at random means that the density function is constant on S).
(a) Determine the joint density function for x and y in S
(with p(x,y) = 0 for all (x,y) not in S.)
(b) If T is a subset of S with area a, find the probability that a point (x,y) is in T.

static.solution:
(a) The area of S is \frac12 (4)(2) = 4. Because the density function p(x,y) is constant on S and the total volume under a density function above the xy-plane is 1, p(x,y) = 1/4 for (x,y) in S, and p(x,y) = 0 for (x,y) outside S.
(b) The probability that (x,y) is in T is \int_T p(x,y)\,dy\,dx = {1\over 4}\quad\int_T\,dy\,dx = {\mbox{area}(T)\over 4} = \frac{a}{4}.
